title: English Practice Quiz 0883
description: A ten-question English practice quiz covering grammar, vocabulary and practical communication.

questions.question: A customer says a service was delayed. The best first response is:
options: I apologise for the delay. Let me check the status.
questions.explanation: Acknowledge the concern and offer to investigate.

questions.question: To 'resolve' a complaint means to:
questions.explanation: Resolve means settle or solve a problem.

questions.question: Which question helps clarify a complaint?
options: Could you explain when the issue first occurred?
questions.explanation: An open, neutral question gathers relevant details.

questions.question: A customer is speaking angrily. You should:
questions.explanation: Calm listening helps identify the concern and de-escalate tension.

questions.question: 'We will look into the matter' means:
Which response avoids making an unsupported promise?
options: It will definitely be fixed in five minutes.
I will check with the team and update you.
You will never face this again.
questions.explanation: It commits to a realistic next step without promising an unknown outcome.

questions.question: A complaint should be escalated when:
options: it requires authority beyond your role
the customer asks a simple question
questions.explanation: Escalation is appropriate when the issue exceeds your authority.

questions.question: Choose the most empathetic phrase.
options: I understand why this is frustrating.
questions.explanation: It recognises the customer's feelings without dismissing them.

questions.question: A service recovery action is intended to:
options: restore customer confidence after a failure
questions.explanation: Service recovery addresses a failure and rebuilds trust.

questions.question: After resolving a complaint, it is useful to:
options: confirm the customer understands the outcome
questions.explanation: Confirming the outcome ensures the resolution is understood.
